name: Seabrook Railroad Bridge
facts: The Seabrook Railroad Bridge, a 1920s bascule marvel, once carried both trains and cars until the 1967 opening of the higher Seabrook Bridge, after which it became a rail‑only crossing.
With a 79‑foot horizontal clearance and unlimited vertical clearance when fully retracted, the bridge keeps the Inner Harbor‑Navigational Canal flowing beneath during high‑wind or flood events.
When a hurricane threatens, the Seabrook Railroad Bridge remains raised to allow waterway traffic, and any lowering requires operators to broadcast on VHF 13 for coordination.
